title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第30部分：模型内部

chapters.History: 1. 我们是怎么走到这里的
chapters.Induction: 5. 一个归纳回路，从头到尾
chapters.Disagree: 17. 这个领域在哪里有分歧

a547c098736d.en: Part by part, we've built every piece of these models ourselves. We know every number in them. And yet we can't say what they're thinking. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's our transformer reading a line of the passage: for each character, the hundred and twenty-eight numbers it carries after its second block. Every one of them busy, all the time; not one of them means anything by itself. <bookmark mark='b'/> This part is about reading them. <bookmark mark='c'/> Rewritten in the right basis, the picture changes: only a handful of features, ideas the model tracks, are on at each character, and each one turns out to mean something.
a547c098736d.zh: 一部分接一部分，这些模型的每个零件，我们都亲手搭过。里面的每一个数字，我们都知道。可我们还是说不出，它在想什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是我们的Transformer在读测试段落里的一行：对每个字符，它在第二个块之后带着的128个数。每一个数都一直在忙，可没有哪一个数，单独拿出来有什么意义。<bookmark mark='b'/>这一部分，讲的就是怎么读懂它们。<bookmark mark='c'/>换到合适的基底里重写，画面就变了：每个字符上，只有少数几个特征亮着，也就是模型在追踪的想法，而每一个，结果都有意义。

b74ebef6bef4.en: Take one character. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its hundred and twenty-eight numbers, tangled together, become 3 features out of five hundred and twelve. <bookmark mark='f'/> A feature is one idea the model tracks, like 'inside a quotation', stored as a direction among those numbers. How far the vector points that way, its shadow on that direction, is how strongly the feature is on.
b74ebef6bef4.zh: 拿一个字符来看。<bookmark mark='a'/>它那128个缠在一起的数，变成了512个特征里的3个。<bookmark mark='f'/>一个特征，就是模型追踪的一个想法，比如“在引号里面”，它以一个方向的形式，存在这些数当中。向量朝那个方向指了多远，也就是它在这个方向上的投影，就是这个特征亮得有多强。

3c5b6a7d6fc2.en: This is Part 30 of AI, Built: inside the model. <bookmark mark='a'/> First, how the field got here, from saliency maps to circuits. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then reading information out of a model, and the traps in doing it; <bookmark mark='c'/> then finding what actually causes a behaviour, down to one circuit end to end. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then why the numbers are tangled, and the dictionaries that untangle them; <bookmark mark='e'/> tracing a prediction from input to output, comparing a model with its fine-tune, and steering. <bookmark mark='f'/> And to finish: grokking explained, whether a chain of thought tells the truth, and where the field stands, and argues, in 2026. Every experiment runs on this computer, most of them on the series' own models.
3c5b6a7d6fc2.zh: 这里是《人工智能，从零搭建》第30部分：模型内部。<bookmark mark='a'/>先讲这个领域是怎么走到今天的，从显著图到回路。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后讲怎么从模型里把信息读出来，以及其中的陷阱；<bookmark mark='c'/>再讲怎么找出真正导致某个行为的原因，一直追到一个完整的回路。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后讲这些数为什么缠在一起，以及把它们解开的字典；<bookmark mark='e'/>把一次预测从输入追到输出，把一个模型和它的微调版本做比较，还有引导。<bookmark mark='f'/>最后讲：顿悟是怎么回事，思维链说的是不是真话，以及到2026年，这个领域走到了哪里，又在争论什么。每个实验都在这台电脑上跑，大多数用的是本系列自己的模型。

79554faf59d2.en: Chapter one. How we got here.
79554faf59d2.zh: 第1章。我们是怎么走到这里的。

a1729cf34e32.en: The first question people asked of a trained network was the simplest: which parts of the input mattered? <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2013 Karen Simonyan, Andrea Vedaldi and Andrew Zisserman took the gradient of a class score with respect to the pixels: a saliency map. Here it is for our character transformer, about to write 'd' after 'she sai'. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each bar is the gradient times the input, the first-order guess of what each character contributes. <bookmark mark='c'/> A blunter test, from Matthew Zeiler and Rob Fergus a year later: blank out one character at a time, and measure how far the score drops. <bookmark mark='d'/> If both told the truth they would agree. Ranked, they barely agree: a correlation of 0.21 here, and 0.07 on average over 24 more predictions. The gradient is a local slope; the network is not a straight line.
a1729cf34e32.zh: 人们对一个训练好的网络提出的第一个问题，也是最简单的：输入里哪些部分重要？<bookmark mark='a'/>2013年，卡伦·西蒙尼扬、安德烈亚·韦达尔迪和安德鲁·齐瑟曼，对类别得分求它相对于像素的梯度：这就是显著图。这里是我们的字符Transformer的显著图，它正要在“she sai”后面写出“d”。<bookmark mark='b'/>每根柱子是梯度乘以输入，是对每个字符贡献的一阶估计。<bookmark mark='c'/>一年后，马修·泽勒和罗布·弗格斯给出了一个更直接的测试：一次遮住一个字符，看得分掉了多少。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果两者都说了真话，它们应该一致。按排名比较，它们几乎不一致：这里的相关系数是0.21，再算24个预测，平均是0.07。梯度只是局部的斜率；网络并不是一条直线。

76718e496458.en: Worse, a picture that looks sensible can explain nothing. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2018 Julius Adebayo and colleagues re-randomized a network's weights, layer by layer from the top, and found that some popular saliency methods barely changed: they were showing the input's edges, not the network's reasons. <bookmark mark='b'/> Run the test on ours. Re-randomize block four, then three and four, and so on down to the embedding, and compare each map with the trained one. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ours passes: by the end the correlation is -0.09, and -0.05 on average over the 24 other predictions. The map does depend on what the network learned. But passing a sanity check is not the same as being right.
76718e496458.zh: 更糟的是，一张看上去合理的图，可能什么也没解释。<bookmark mark='a'/>2018年，朱利叶斯·阿德巴约和同事把一个网络的权重从顶层开始一层层重新随机化，结果发现，一些流行的显著图方法几乎没变：它们显示的是输入的边缘，而不是网络的理由。<bookmark mark='b'/>在我们的模型上也做这个测试。重新随机化第4块，然后第3和第4块，一直到嵌入层，再把每张图和训练好的那张比较。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的模型通过了：到最后，相关系数是-0.09，在另外24个预测上平均是-0.05。这张图确实取决于网络学到了什么。但通过了合理性检查，并不等于是对的。

124e6bb30eef.en: So the question moved from which inputs to what the parts of a network are for. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2015 Alexander Mordvintsev, Chris Olah and Mike Tyka ran the gradient the other way, changing an image to excite a layer, and DeepDream's dog-filled clouds went around the world. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2017 David Bau's Network Dissection scored every unit against labelled concepts, and found units for lamps and for dogs. <bookmark mark='c'/> The same year Olah, Mordvintsev and Ludwig Schubert turned the trick into a science in the online journal Distill: feature visualization, an input optimized until one neuron fires. <bookmark mark='d'/> A year later they combined it with attribution: what the network sees, and where.
124e6bb30eef.zh: 于是问题从“哪些输入重要”，转到了“网络的各个部分是干什么的”。<bookmark mark='a'/>2015年，亚历山大·莫尔德温采夫、克里斯·奥拉和迈克·泰卡让梯度反过来走，改变一张图像去激发某一层，DeepDream那些长满狗的云就传遍了世界。<bookmark mark='b'/>2017年，戴维·鲍的“网络解剖”把每个单元和带标签的概念逐一打分，找到了对应台灯的单元，也找到了对应狗的单元。<bookmark mark='c'/>同一年，奥拉、莫尔德温采夫和路德维希·舒伯特在在线期刊Distill上，把这个技巧做成了一门学问：特征可视化，也就是优化一个输入，直到某个神经元被激发。<bookmark mark='d'/>一年后，他们把它和归因结合起来：网络看到了什么，又是在哪里看到的。

c27bb0d2ebda.en: In 2020 the work found its programme. Olah and colleagues' Zoom In made three speculative claims. <bookmark mark='a'/> Features are the units of a network; features connect through weights into circuits; and the same features and circuits turn up in different models. They traced curve detectors in a vision network wire by wire. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the programme moved to language. In 2021, multimodal neurons in CLIP, and a mathematical framework for transformer circuits; <bookmark mark='c'/> in 2022, induction heads, a 26-head circuit in GPT-2 small, and toy models of superposition, which explained why single neurons so rarely mean one thing. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then sparse dictionaries split neurons into features, first in a one-layer model, then by the million in Claude 3 Sonnet, and in 2025 attribution graphs traced a production model's computations. This part walks that path on our own models.
c27bb0d2ebda.zh: 2020年，这项工作有了自己的纲领。奥拉和同事的《放大》提出了三个推测性的主张。<bookmark mark='a'/>特征是网络的基本单元；特征通过权重连成回路；同样的特征和回路，会出现在不同的模型里。他们在一个视觉网络里，一根线一根线地追出了曲线检测器。<bookmark mark='b'/>接着，这套纲领转向了语言。2021年，有了CLIP里的多模态神经元，还有一套关于Transformer回路的数学框架；<bookmark mark='c'/>2022年，有了归纳头，有了GPT-2 small里一个由26个头组成的回路，还有叠加的玩具模型，它解释了为什么单个神经元很少只表示一件事。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后，稀疏字典把神经元拆成了特征，先是在一个单层模型里，然后在Claude 3 Sonnet里成百万地拆；2025年，归因图追踪了一个生产级模型的计算过程。这一部分，就在我们自己的模型上，把这条路走一遍。

23a30b3c1f75.en: Chapter two. What does it know?

0ba33bb36354.en: Saliency asks where the model looked. A probe asks what it knows. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a property of the text, say, whether the reader is inside a quotation at this token: the novels model, Part 18's six-layer transformer, must track it to know when a closing quote is coming. <bookmark mark='b'/> A probe is a small classifier, trained to read that property off one layer's vectors. If a linear probe succeeds, the information is sitting there along a direction. <bookmark mark='c'/> Guillaume Alain and Yoshua Bengio put linear probes on every layer of a network in 2016, and probing became the first workhorse of interpretability.
0ba33bb36354.zh: 显著图问的是模型看了哪里。探针问的是它知道什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>拿文本的一个性质来说，比如：读到这个词元时，读者是不是在引号里面。小说模型，也就是第18部分那个六层的Transformer，必须追踪这件事，才知道什么时候该出现后引号。<bookmark mark='b'/>探针就是一个小分类器，训练它从某一层的向量里读出这个性质。如果一个线性探针能做到，说明这个信息就沿着某个方向放在那里。<bookmark mark='c'/>2016年，纪尧姆·阿兰和约书亚·本吉奥在一个网络的每一层上都放了线性探针，探测就成了可解释性的第一匹“老黄牛”。

6fb182ed6ccb.en: We trained a linear probe on each layer of the novels model, with three seeds. <bookmark mark='a'/> Guessing the commoner label scores 61 percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> At the token embedding, before any attention, the probe reaches 66 percent: a token alone says little about where it sits. <bookmark mark='c'/> After a few blocks it reaches 91 percent, at layer 5: attention has carried the quotation marks forward, and the state is written along a direction.
6fb182ed6ccb.zh: 我们在小说模型的每一层上训练了一个线性探针，用了三个种子。<bookmark mark='a'/>总是猜那个更常见的标签，能得61%。<bookmark mark='b'/>在词元嵌入上，还没有经过任何注意力，探针能到66%：光看一个词元，说明不了它在什么位置。<bookmark mark='c'/>经过几个块之后，它在第5层达到91%：注意力把引号的信息带了过来，这个状态沿着一个方向写了下来。

5987402803ce.en: But who did the work, the model or the probe? <bookmark mark='a'/> John Hewitt and Percy Liang's control task asks it directly. Give every token type a random label, at the same rate; there is no such property in the text, so a probe that scores well has simply memorized which tokens carry which label. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the embedding the control is easy: each token is its own vector. Our linear probe gets 80 percent of the nonsense right there, against 66 on the real task. <bookmark mark='p'/> Pause and predict: a more powerful probe, a small MLP, can fit more. Will it be more selective, or less? <bookmark mark='c'/> The MLP probe scores higher on the task, 91 percent against 91, <bookmark mark='c2'/>but it also learns the nonsense better: at layer 5 its selectivity is 3 points, the linear probe's 16. A more powerful probe tells you more about the probe. <bookmark mark='d'/> Selectivity, the task minus the control, is what a probe result should be reported with.
5987402803ce.zh: 可活到底是谁干的，模型还是探针？<bookmark mark='a'/>约翰·休伊特和Percy Liang的对照任务，直接问的就是这个。给每一种词元随机分配一个标签，比例不变；文本里根本没有这种性质，所以一个探针要是得分很高，只说明它记住了哪些词元带哪个标签。<bookmark mark='b'/>在嵌入层上，对照任务很容易：每个词元都是它自己的向量。我们的线性探针在那里能答对80%的瞎标签，真任务是66%。<bookmark mark='p'/>暂停一下，预测一下：一个更强的探针，一个小MLP，能拟合更多东西。它的选择性会更高，还是更低？<bookmark mark='c'/>MLP探针在真任务上得分更高，91%对91%，<bookmark mark='c2'/>但它也更会学那些瞎标签：在第5层，它的选择性是3个百分点，线性探针是16。探针越强，告诉你的就越是探针自己的事。<bookmark mark='d'/>选择性，也就是真任务减去对照任务，才是报告探针结果时应该附上的数。

2ea1830e8396.en: There is a second trap. A probe shows that information can be read; not that the model reads it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Yanai Elazar and colleagues' answer: remove what the probe reads, and see whether the model notices. We take the linear probe's direction at layer 5, project it out of every vector, and run the rest of the model. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the tokens that close a quotation, predicting them costs 4.03 bits as the model is. <bookmark mark='c'/> Removing ten random directions instead costs 4.04. <bookmark mark='d'/> Removing the probe's direction costs 5.59. The model was using that direction to know a quote was open. Reading out is correlation; changing the model and watching is causation, the subject of chapter four.
2ea1830e8396.zh: 还有第二个陷阱。探针说明信息可以被读出来；并不说明模型自己读了它。<bookmark mark='a'/>亚奈·埃拉扎尔和同事的回答是：把探针读的东西去掉，看模型有没有察觉。我们取第5层线性探针的方向，从每个向量里把它投影掉，再让模型跑完剩下的部分。<bookmark mark='b'/>在那些结束引号的词元上，模型原本预测它们要花4.03比特。<bookmark mark='c'/>换成去掉十个随机方向，要花4.04比特。<bookmark mark='d'/>去掉探针的方向，要花5.59比特。模型确实在用这个方向，来知道引号还开着。读出来，是相关；改动模型再看结果，才是因果，这是第4章的主题。

6c16fee6e7b4.en: Chapter three. Reading the stream as it flows.
6c16fee6e7b4.zh: 第3章。读出流动中的残差流。

eaf4f3294edc.en: A probe is trained. There is a reading you get for free. <bookmark mark='a'/> In a transformer, every block reads the residual stream and adds its result back. The last step of the model turns the final stream into a prediction: a normalization, then the unembedding matrix. <bookmark mark='b'/> So apply that last step early, to the stream after every block, and ask what the model would say if it stopped there. <bookmark mark='c'/> A pseudonymous writer, nostalgebraist, tried it on GPT-2 in 2020 and called it the logit lens.
eaf4f3294edc.zh: 探针需要训练。还有一种读法，是白送的。<bookmark mark='a'/>在Transformer里，每个块读一遍残差流，再把结果加回去。模型的最后一步，把最终的残差流变成预测：先做一次归一化，再乘上反嵌入矩阵。<bookmark mark='b'/>那就把这最后一步提前，用在每个块之后的残差流上，问一问：如果模型在这里停下，它会说什么？<bookmark mark='c'/>2020年，一位化名nostalgebraist的作者在GPT-2上试了这件事，把它叫作logit透镜。

88387954eab1.en: Here is the logit lens on the novels model, reading 'it was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of'. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each row is a layer, each column a position, and each cell the lens's best guess for the next token. <bookmark mark='b'/> At the bottom, the embedding alone mostly guesses tokens that often follow the current one, and the guesses are poor. <bookmark mark='c'/> Going up, the right continuations firm up; at the last position, the final guess, 'the', is already the top guess at layer 1. Predictions are built gradually, refined block by block.
88387954eab1.zh: 这是小说模型上的logit透镜，它读的是“it was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of”。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一行是一层，每一列是一个位置，每一格是透镜对下一个词元的最佳猜测。<bookmark mark='b'/>在最底下，只有嵌入的时候，它多半猜的是常跟在当前词元后面的词元，而且猜得很差。<bookmark mark='c'/>越往上，正确的接续越来越确定；在最后一个位置，最终的猜测“the”，在第1层就已经排第一了。预测是一点一点搭起来的，一个块一个块地修正。

5fa7341b2f99.en: The logit lens assumes every layer speaks the last layer's language. It doesn't quite: early layers store things in other directions. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2023 Nora Belrose and colleagues added a translator: one affine map per layer, trained so the lens matches the model's final prediction. <bookmark mark='b'/> We trained one for each layer of the novels model. They start as the logit lens, <bookmark mark='c'/> and over 300 steps the gap to the final prediction falls at every layer, most at the bottom, where the logit lens is furthest off.
5fa7341b2f99.zh: logit透镜假定每一层都说最后一层的语言。其实不完全是：前面几层会把东西存在别的方向上。<bookmark mark='a'/>2023年，诺拉·贝尔罗斯和同事加了一个翻译器：每层一个仿射映射，训练它让透镜对上模型的最终预测。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们给小说模型的每一层都训练了一个。它们一开始就是logit透镜，<bookmark mark='c'/>经过300步训练，每一层和最终预测的差距都在下降，最底下降得最多，那里logit透镜偏得最远。

fdf60a1ba1d8.en: Held out, the comparison is clear. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the embedding, the logit lens is 8.6 bits away from the final prediction, the tuned lens 2.5. <bookmark mark='b'/> Halfway up, 1.9 against 1.1. Measured as a predictor of the next token, the embedding read by the logit lens costs 13.6 bits per token, by the tuned lens 7.6, and the model itself 5.3. <bookmark mark='c'/> A lens is still a reading, not a mind: it shows what a linear readout could take from each layer, and the same caveats as a probe apply.
fdf60a1ba1d8.zh: 在留出的文本上，对比很清楚。<bookmark mark='a'/>在嵌入层，logit透镜离最终预测有8.6比特，调校透镜是2.5。<bookmark mark='b'/>到一半的高度，是1.9对1.1。把它们当作下一个词元的预测器来量：用logit透镜读嵌入层，每个词元要13.6比特，用调校透镜是7.6，模型本身是5.3。<bookmark mark='c'/>透镜终究是一种读法，不是心智：它显示的是，从每一层用线性方式能读出什么，探针的那些注意事项在这里同样适用。

f8a0fdeaf3bd.en: To find what causes a behaviour, you need a behaviour with a known answer. The classic is copying: show a model a passage twice, and the second time it should be easy, since the model can look back. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 13's character transformer: 1.79 bits per character the first time, 1.80 the second. <bookmark mark='b'/> The novels model: 5.18 bits per token, then 5.07. Neither of our models copies. Olsson and colleagues saw the heads that copy form in their models between about 2.5 and 5 billion tokens of training; ours stopped at about 25 million. <bookmark mark='c'/> So for a circuit to take apart, we go back to Part 13's two-layer, attention-only model, trained on random tokens with one stretch repeated, where copying is the only thing worth learning.
f8a0fdeaf3bd.zh: 要找出一个行为的原因，得先有一个答案已知的行为。经典的例子是复制：给模型看同一段文字两遍，第二遍应该很容易，因为模型可以往回看。<bookmark mark='a'/>第13部分的字符Transformer：第一遍每字符1.79比特，第二遍1.80。<bookmark mark='b'/>小说模型：每词元5.18比特，然后是5.07。我们的两个模型都不会复制。奥尔森和同事看到，在他们的模型里，负责复制的头大约在训练到25亿到50亿个词元之间形成；我们的模型只训练了大约25百万个词元。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以，要找一个可以拆开的回路，我们回到第13部分那个两层、只有注意力的模型：它在随机词元上训练，其中有一段被重复了一遍，复制是唯一值得学的东西。

e52b76cb6c90.en: We retrain it here with Part 13's recipe and seed. <bookmark mark='a'/> For a while it learns nothing useful; then, suddenly, the repeat becomes easy, falling from 6.2 to 1.5 bits per token while random tokens stay as hard as ever. <bookmark mark='b'/> Look at the attention. In layer one, 2 of the four heads look mostly at the previous token; here is head 1. <bookmark mark='c'/> In layer two, 3 heads, at a token in the second copy, look at the token just after that token's first occurrence: the one to copy. Previous-token heads and induction heads. But attention patterns are a correlation too. Are these heads the cause?
e52b76cb6c90.zh: 我们在这里用第13部分的配方和种子重新训练它。<bookmark mark='a'/>有一阵子，它什么有用的都没学到；然后，突然之间，重复的部分变得容易了，从每词元6.2比特降到1.5，而随机的词元还是一样难。<bookmark mark='b'/>看看注意力。在第一层，四个头里有2个主要看前一个词元；这是第1个头。<bookmark mark='c'/>在第二层，有3个头，在第二遍里的某个词元上，看的是这个词元第一次出现时紧跟在后面的那个词元：也就是要复制的那个。前一词元头，和归纳头。可注意力模式也只是相关。这些头是原因吗？

4f14f71f9222.en: The tool is activation patching. <bookmark mark='a'/> Run the model twice: on the clean sequence, with its repeat, and on a corrupted one, the first copy replaced by fresh random tokens, so there is nothing to copy. Then take one vector from the corrupted run, put it into the clean run, and see how much of the right prediction at position 70 is lost. Kevin Meng and colleagues used patching to find where GPT stores facts. <bookmark mark='b'/> Swap the residual stream at every position, at the input, between the layers, and at the output. At the input, breaking position 20, 21 breaks the copy. <bookmark mark='c'/> Between the layers, 21, 70. <bookmark mark='d'/> At the output, only position 70 itself. The information about what to copy starts at the first copy, moves one step within it, and then jumps to the second copy: that is the circuit's route.
4f14f71f9222.zh: 用的工具是激活修补。<bookmark mark='a'/>让模型跑两次：一次在干净的序列上，带着它的重复；一次在被破坏的序列上，第一遍被换成新的随机词元，于是没东西可复制。然后从被破坏的那次运行里取一个向量，放进干净的那次运行，看第70个位置上正确的预测损失了多少。凯文·孟和同事就是用修补的方法，找到GPT把事实存在哪里。<bookmark mark='b'/>在每一个位置上替换残差流：在输入处，在两层之间，在输出处。在输入处，破坏第20, 21个位置，复制就被破坏了。<bookmark mark='c'/>在两层之间，是21, 70。<bookmark mark='d'/>在输出处，只有第70个位置本身。关于“复制什么”的信息，从第一遍开始，在其中挪动一步，然后跳到第二遍：这就是回路走的路线。

12a8485924e3.en: Now the heads: run the clean sequence, and swap in one head's output from the corrupted run. <bookmark mark='a'/> Corrupting one of the previous-token heads loses 29 to 39 percent of the copying; the induction heads, 29 to 46. <bookmark mark='b'/> And one more head matters, head 4 of layer one, which mostly looks at the token itself: 65 percent. No other head more than 13. A small team of heads carries the behaviour. Chapter five takes it apart.
12a8485924e3.zh: 再来看头：跑干净的序列，把某一个头的输出换成被破坏那次运行里的。<bookmark mark='a'/>破坏其中一个前一词元头，复制能力损失29%到39%；归纳头是29%到46%。<bookmark mark='b'/>还有一个头也很重要，第一层的第4个头，它主要看词元自己：65%。其他的头，都不超过13%。这个行为由一小组头承担。第5章把它拆开来看。

00f109301598.en: Chapter five. An induction circuit, end to end.
00f109301598.zh: 第5章。一个归纳回路，从头到尾。

9cbea2945868.en: Two heads in different layers can only work together through the residual stream: the first writes, the second reads. <bookmark mark='a'/> But the second head reads in three places, its queries, its keys and its values. Which one carries the message? Pause and predict. <bookmark mark='p'/> Path patching asks exactly that: send the corrupted outputs of the previous-token heads into one of the three only, and leave everything else clean. <bookmark mark='b'/> Into the queries: 0 percent of the copying lost. Into the values: 1. <bookmark mark='c'/> Into the keys: 86. The message goes through the keys. Each token's key now carries the token before it, so the induction heads' query, the current token, finds the position right after its last occurrence. <bookmark mark='d'/>Either previous-token head alone carries 29 to 39 percent: they share the job. And the head that looks at the token itself sends its message mostly into the queries, 49 percent: the query says which token we are at.
9cbea2945868.zh: 不同层里的两个头，只能通过残差流合作：第一个写，第二个读。<bookmark mark='a'/>可第二个头在三个地方读：它的查询、它的键、它的值。消息是从哪一个传过去的？暂停一下，预测一下。<bookmark mark='p'/>路径修补问的正是这个：把前一词元头被破坏的输出，只送进这三处中的一处，其余一切保持干净。<bookmark mark='b'/>送进查询：复制能力损失0%。送进值：1%。<bookmark mark='c'/>送进键：86%。消息走的是键。现在每个词元的键里都带着它前面那个词元，于是归纳头的查询，也就是当前词元，能找到它上一次出现之后紧挨着的那个位置。<bookmark mark='d'/>任何一个前一词元头单独承担29%到39%：它们分担这份工作。那个看词元自己的头，消息主要送进查询，49%：查询说明我们在哪个词元上。

97d8a94a96e7.en: The same fact is written in the weights, before running anything. <bookmark mark='a'/> The second head compares queries and keys through one matrix, W Q K. <bookmark mark='b'/> The first head writes into the stream through another, W O V. <bookmark mark='c'/> Their composition score, from Nelson Elhage and colleagues' framework, asks how much of what the first head writes the second head's keys can read. <bookmark mark='d'/> From our previous-token heads into our induction heads it is 0.17 to 0.19; for random heads of the same shape it would be 0.124, give or take 0.007: at least 7 standard deviations away. The keys were built to read those heads.
97d8a94a96e7.zh: 同样的事实，在什么都还没跑之前，就写在权重里了。<bookmark mark='a'/>第二个头通过一个矩阵W QK来比较查询和键。<bookmark mark='b'/>第一个头通过另一个矩阵W OV往残差流里写。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们的组合分数，来自纳尔逊·埃尔哈格和同事的框架，问的是：第一个头写下的东西，第二个头的键能读到多少。<bookmark mark='d'/>从我们的前一词元头到归纳头，组合分数在0.17到0.19之间；同样形状的随机头，会是0.124，上下浮动0.007：至少相差7个标准差。这些键，就是为了读那些头而长成的。

95d0dfb8db25.en: Each head's job can be read off its weights too. <bookmark mark='a'/> Feed the previous-token heads nothing but the position embeddings: the scores are highest for the token itself and the one before it, and fall off with distance: position narrows attention to the last few tokens, and the tokens' content does the rest. <bookmark mark='b'/> And trace the induction heads' values all the way from the token they attend to, through W O V, to the logits: a 64 by 64 matrix, token in, logit out. <bookmark mark='c'/> For 83 percent of tokens, the logit raised most is the token's own, and the eigenvalues give a copying score of 0.88, where 1 would be pure copying. The heads copy.
95d0dfb8db25.zh: 每个头的工作，也能从它的权重里读出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>只给前一词元头输入位置嵌入：分数最高的是词元自己和它前面那个，然后随距离衰减：位置把注意力收窄到最近的几个词元，剩下的由词元的内容来完成。<bookmark mark='b'/>再把归纳头的值，从它们关注的词元出发，经过W OV，一路追到logit：一个64乘64的矩阵，词元进，logit出。<bookmark mark='c'/>对83%的词元来说，提升最多的logit就是这个词元自己的，特征值给出的复制分数是0.88，1代表纯粹的复制。这些头在复制。

8b24b09e3751.en: Last, the bluntest test: remove each head, replacing its output by its average. <bookmark mark='a'/> With every head in place the repeat costs 1.49 bits per token. <bookmark mark='b'/> Without a previous-token head, up to 2.66; without an induction head, up to 3.55; without the current-token head, 3.59; random tokens with nothing to copy cost 6.20. The circuit, end to end: heads in layer one write each token's predecessor into it, a head there sharpens which token is which, and the induction heads find the match through their keys and copy it through their values.
8b24b09e3751.zh: 最后，最直接的测试：把每个头去掉，用它的平均输出代替。<bookmark mark='a'/>所有头都在的时候，重复部分每词元要1.49比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>去掉一个前一词元头，最多到2.66；去掉一个归纳头，最多到3.55；去掉看词元自己的那个头，3.59；没东西可复制的随机词元，要6.20。整个回路从头到尾是这样的：第一层的几个头把每个词元的前一个写进它里面，那里还有一个头让“哪个词元是哪个”更清楚，归纳头再通过它们的键找到匹配，通过它们的值把它复制过来。

bd29621e9deb.en: Part 13 watched these heads form. Now we can watch the cause form. Replay the training, and at every checkpoint measure the keys path, the effect of corrupting the previous-token head's message into the induction head's keys alone. <bookmark mark='a'/> The loss on the repeat falls fastest around step 2,600. <bookmark mark='b'/> The keys path switches on at the same moment, around step 2,750: the drop in the loss is the circuit being completed.
bd29621e9deb.zh: 第13部分看着这些头形成。现在我们可以看着原因形成。重放训练过程，在每个检查点测量键这条路径：只把前一词元头的消息，破坏后送进归纳头的键，看效果有多大。<bookmark mark='a'/>重复部分的损失，大约在第2600步降得最快。<bookmark mark='b'/>键这条路径就在同一时刻打开，大约在第2750步：损失的骤降，就是回路的完工。

30114e342c0f.en: Chapter six. More ideas than dimensions.

57fb8b6d3c52.en: Here's the smallest model that shows why. Five features go in, squeezed through just two numbers, and the network must give all five back: x hat equals ReLU of W transpose W x, plus b. <bookmark mark='w'/> In words: W squeezes the five numbers into two, the same W run backwards spreads them out to five again, and the ReLU cuts off anything negative. The features matter unequally, the brighter ones more. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each column of W says where a feature points in the two-dimensional middle. <bookmark mark='b'/> When every feature is on all the time, the trained network keeps just the 2 most important, at right angles, and drops the rest. <bookmark mark='c'/> Make the features rarer, and it starts to cheat: 4 features, in opposite pairs. <bookmark mark='d'/> Rarer still, and all 5 fit, as a pentagon. Five ideas in two dimensions. That's superposition.
57fb8b6d3c52.zh: 这里有一个能说明原因的最小模型。五个特征进去，挤过区区两个数，网络必须把五个都还回来：x帽等于ReLU作用在W转置乘W乘x加b上。<bookmark mark='w'/>换句话说：W把五个数挤成两个，同一个W反过来用，再把它们摊回五个，ReLU把负的部分切掉。这些特征重要性不同，越亮的越重要。<bookmark mark='a'/>W的每一列，说明一个特征在中间那个二维空间里指向哪里。<bookmark mark='b'/>当每个特征一直都开着时，训练好的网络只保留最重要的2个，互相垂直，其余的丢掉。<bookmark mark='c'/>让特征变得稀少一些，它就开始“作弊”：4个特征，两两相对。<bookmark mark='d'/>再稀少一些，全部5个都放得下，排成一个五边形。两维里装下五个想法。这就是叠加。

42c3b439b66d.en: How does the network find that pentagon? Here is the sparse model learning, from its random start. <bookmark mark='a'/> At first the five arrows point anywhere, some short, some long. <bookmark mark='b'/> Within a few hundred steps they all grow, and they push each other apart: two features pointing the same way would be read as each other. <bookmark mark='c'/> By step 250 the spacing is even, and the rest of training barely moves them. Nobody planned the pentagon; gradient descent found it, fast.
42c3b439b66d.zh: 网络是怎么找到这个五边形的？这里是那个稀疏模型从随机初始状态开始的学习过程。<bookmark mark='a'/>一开始，五个箭头随便指，有的短，有的长。<bookmark mark='b'/>几百步之内，它们都变长了，而且互相推开：两个指向相同的特征，会被当成彼此。<bookmark mark='c'/>到第250步，间隔就均匀了，之后的训练几乎不再移动它们。没人设计这个五边形；是梯度下降找到的，而且很快。

19bf55011b93.en: But packing has a price. Turn on feature one alone. <bookmark mark='a'/> Reading it back out, every other feature sees its shadow along their direction. <bookmark mark='b'/> The neighbours, at about 73 degrees, get a little; the far ones, at about 145, get a negative amount. <bookmark mark='c'/> The bias pushes everything down a little, <bookmark mark='d'/> and the ReLU throws away whatever is negative. What's left over is small: a little noise, the cost of sharing space. It's worth paying only because the features are rarely on together.
19bf55011b93.zh: 可是挤在一起是有代价的。只打开特征1。<bookmark mark='a'/>把它读回来时，其他每个特征都会在自己的方向上看到它的影子。<bookmark mark='b'/>相邻的，大约在73度，得到一点点；远的，大约在145度，得到一个负值。<bookmark mark='c'/>偏置把所有东西都往下压一点，<bookmark mark='d'/>ReLU把负的全部扔掉。剩下的很小：一点噪声，这是共享空间的代价。之所以值得付，只因为这些特征很少同时出现。

e4d5eadf8a88.en: Chapter six showed superposition happen. Elhage and colleagues asked when it happens, and drew the answer as a phase diagram. <bookmark mark='a'/> The smallest case: two features, squeezed through a single number. Feature two matters r times as much as feature one, and each is on a fraction rho of the time. <bookmark mark='b'/> The network has three choices. Drop feature two. <bookmark mark='c'/> Give feature two the dimension and drop feature one. <bookmark mark='d'/> Or share: point the two features in opposite directions, and let the ReLU, with a negative bias, cut off each one's shadow on the other. Sharing only pays when they are rarely on at the same time.
e4d5eadf8a88.zh: 第6章看到了叠加的发生。埃尔哈格和同事问的是：它什么时候发生？他们把答案画成了一张相图。<bookmark mark='a'/>最小的情形：两个特征，挤过一个数。特征2的重要性是特征1的r倍，每个特征出现的时间比例是ρ。<bookmark mark='b'/>网络有三种选择。丢掉特征2。<bookmark mark='c'/>把这个维度给特征2，丢掉特征1。<bookmark mark='d'/>或者共享：让两个特征指向相反的方向，再让ReLU加上一个负的偏置，把彼此的影子切掉。只有当它们很少同时出现时，共享才划算。

157ab35f6c3f.en: We trained the little model on a grid of 17 densities by 17 importances, four seeds a cell, and kept the best. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each cell is coloured by what the trained network did with feature two; here is one cell's training, the two weights settling into opposite signs. <bookmark mark='b'/> When features are dense, at the top, the network shares in 0 of the top row's 17 cells: one feature gets the dimension, the other is dropped. <bookmark mark='c'/> When features are sparse, at the bottom, sharing wins across 17 of 17 cells. <bookmark mark='d'/> On the right, the same map from theory: for every cell, the expected loss of each of the three choices, and the cheapest. They agree on 94 percent of the cells, and the misses sit on the boundaries, where two choices cost almost the same. Superposition is a phase the network enters when features are sparse enough.
157ab35f6c3f.zh: 我们在一个网格上训练这个小模型：17种密度乘17种重要性，每格四个种子，留下最好的。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一格的颜色，表示训练好的网络对特征2做了什么；这里是其中一格的训练过程，两个权重稳定在相反的符号上。<bookmark mark='b'/>特征密集的时候，也就是最上面一行，17格里只有0格在共享：一个特征得到维度，另一个被丢掉。<bookmark mark='c'/>特征稀疏的时候，也就是最下面一行，共享在17格里赢下了17格。<bookmark mark='d'/>右边是同一张图，来自理论：对每一格，算出三种选择各自的期望损失，取最便宜的那个。两者在94%的格子上一致，不一致的都在边界上，那里两种选择的代价几乎一样。叠加，是特征足够稀疏时，网络进入的一个相。

63e27cdf2107.en: In two dimensions, five features are a crowd. But real models have hundreds or thousands of dimensions, and there, space is roomier than intuition says. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pick two random directions and measure the angle between them. In two dimensions, anything goes. <bookmark mark='b'/> In sixteen, they're usually close to perpendicular; in a hundred and twenty-eight, very close; <bookmark mark='c'/> in a thousand and twenty-four, the cosine is within a few hundredths of zero. The spread shrinks like one over root d, so the number of almost-perpendicular directions grows exponentially with the dimension. That's part three's random projections again, and it's why models can store far more features than they have numbers, as long as each feature is rare.
63e27cdf2107.zh: 在二维里，五个特征就挤了。但真正的模型有成百上千维，在那里，空间比直觉宽敞得多。<bookmark mark='a'/>随便取两个方向，量一量它们之间的夹角。在二维里，什么都有可能。<bookmark mark='b'/>在16维里，它们通常接近垂直；在128维里，非常接近；<bookmark mark='c'/>在1024维里，余弦离零只有几个百分点。它的分散程度按根号d分之1缩小，所以几乎相互垂直的方向，数量随维数指数增长。这又是第3部分的随机投影，也正是模型能存下比自己的数多得多的特征的原因，只要每个特征都很少出现。

438e335772a4.en: Chapter eight. Pulling the features apart.

d08f5f125010.en: If the model stores features as directions, can we find them? The tool is a sparse autoencoder. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the model's vector x at some character, <bookmark mark='b'/> and encode it into many more numbers, five hundred and twelve, with a ReLU so they're never negative. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then rebuild x as a sum of directions, one per feature, weighted by how strongly each is on. <bookmark mark='d'/> Train it to rebuild well, while paying for every feature it uses. That penalty is the whole trick: it forces the code to be sparse, so each vector is explained by a few directions. <bookmark mark='e'/> Trained on 211 thousand vectors from our transformer, it uses about 7 features per character and rebuilds 89 percent of the variance: of all the ways these vectors differ from their average, the rebuild captures 89 percent. Put the rebuild back into the model in place of the real vectors, and it writes at 1.94 bits per character, against 1.72 as it is, and 5.61 with the vectors replaced by their average.
d08f5f125010.zh: 如果模型把特征存成方向，我们能找到它们吗？用的工具是稀疏自编码器。<bookmark mark='a'/>取模型在某个字符上的向量x，<bookmark mark='b'/>把它编码成多得多的数，512个，再加一个ReLU，让它们永远不是负的。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后把x重建成一组方向的和，每个特征一个方向，按每个特征亮的强度加权。<bookmark mark='d'/>训练它重建得好，同时为它用到的每个特征付费。这个惩罚就是全部的诀窍：它逼着编码变得稀疏，让每个向量只用几个方向来解释。<bookmark mark='e'/>用我们Transformer的211千个向量训练之后，它每个字符大约用7个特征，重建了89%的方差：这些向量偏离平均值的所有方式里，重建抓住了89%。把重建放回模型，替换真正的向量，它写字每字符要1.94比特，原样是1.72，把向量换成它们的平均值是5.61。

0899a170dcf6.en: Watch it learn. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the start, with random directions, the penalty has not bitten yet: the character on the right switches on 231 features. <bookmark mark='b'/> As training goes, the penalty prunes, and the rebuild improves at the same time, because the directions turn to face the data. <bookmark mark='c'/> By the end, 3 features describe that character, and the variance left is 11 percent.
0899a170dcf6.zh: 看它学习。<bookmark mark='a'/>一开始，方向是随机的，惩罚还没起作用：右边这个字符打开了231个特征。<bookmark mark='b'/>随着训练，惩罚在修剪，重建同时也在改进，因为这些方向转过来，对准了数据。<bookmark mark='c'/>到最后，3个特征描述这个字符，剩下没解释的方差是11%。

bdc841d02cb1.en: So what are the features? For each one, find where in the novels it fires hardest, and look. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are four. Each lights up on the same kind of moment, again and again. Of the 512 features that ever fire, 498 put at least six of their eight strongest moments on the same character. They're not all this clean, and in a model this small they're mostly about spelling and punctuation. In big models, the same method finds features for cities, for code bugs, for flattery, for the Golden Gate Bridge.
bdc841d02cb1.zh: 那这些特征是什么？对每一个，找出它在小说里亮得最强的地方，看一看。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有四个。每一个都在同一类时刻上亮起来，一次又一次。在512个亮过的特征里，有498个，最强的八个时刻里至少有六个落在同一个字符上。它们并不都这么干净，在这么小的模型里，它们大多跟拼写和标点有关。在大模型里，同样的方法能找到城市的特征、代码漏洞的特征、奉承的特征，还有金门大桥的特征。

2b2d7bbae8e9.en: Why not just read the model's own neurons, the numbers in each MLP's hidden layer, part nine's units? <bookmark mark='a'/> Here's a typical one, from the second block, at its strongest moments: 6 of the eight land on the same character. <bookmark mark='b'/> Count it up: of each unit's eight strongest moments, how many share one character? For neurons, 5.9 on average; for the features, 7.8. The features are cleaner. In a model this small, and this close to its characters, even neurons are fairly clean; in large models, where features are packed in superposition across neurons, single neurons mean many things at once, and the gap is far wider.
2b2d7bbae8e9.zh: 为什么不直接读模型自己的神经元，也就是每个MLP隐藏层里的数，第9部分的那些单元？<bookmark mark='a'/>这是第二个块里一个典型的神经元，在它最强的时刻：八个里有6个落在同一个字符上。<bookmark mark='b'/>数一数：每个单元最强的八个时刻里，有几个落在同一个字符上？神经元平均是5.9个；特征是7.8个。特征更干净。在这么小、又离字符这么近的模型里，连神经元都相当干净；在大模型里，特征以叠加的方式挤在神经元上，单个神经元同时表示很多东西，差距要大得多。

67f521e703fa.en: Chapter eight's autoencoder paid for sparsity with an L1 penalty, and the penalty has a side effect you can derive in three lines. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a single feature whose true size is a, and its code f: the cost is the rebuild error plus lambda times f. <bookmark mark='b'/> Set the slope to zero. <bookmark mark='c'/> The best code is a minus lambda over two: every active feature is shrunk by the same amount, so the rebuild comes out too short. <bookmark mark='d'/> Measured on ours: the factor that would best stretch the rebuild back is 1.04 at the weakest penalty and 1.30 at the strongest.
67f521e703fa.zh: 第8章的自编码器用L1惩罚来换稀疏，而这个惩罚有一个副作用，三行就能推出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>取一个真实大小为a的特征，它的编码是f：代价是重建误差，加上λ乘以f。<bookmark mark='b'/>令斜率为零。<bookmark mark='c'/>最好的编码是a减去λ的一半：每个亮着的特征，都被缩小同样的量，所以重建出来的向量偏短。<bookmark mark='d'/>在我们的模型上量一量：能把重建最好地拉回原长的倍数，惩罚最弱时是1.04，最强时是1.30。

4d108879addb.en: Two fixes came in 2024. <bookmark mark='a'/> Leo Gao and colleagues at OpenAI dropped the penalty: TopK keeps each vector's k largest features and zeroes the rest, so sparsity is set directly and nothing is shrunk. They trained one with sixteen million latents on GPT-4. <bookmark mark='b'/> Senthooran Rajamanoharan and colleagues at DeepMind kept a penalty, but on the count of active features, with a learned threshold per feature: JumpReLU, the recipe behind their open Gemma Scope dictionaries. A step has no gradient, so the threshold is trained through a straight-through estimate.
4d108879addb.zh: 2024年，出现了两种修正。<bookmark mark='a'/>OpenAI的Leo Gao和同事干脆去掉了惩罚：TopK只保留每个向量最大的k个特征，其余归零，于是稀疏程度直接设定，什么都不会被缩小。他们在GPT-4上训练了一个有1600万个潜变量的字典。<bookmark mark='b'/>DeepMind的森图兰·拉贾马诺哈兰和同事保留了惩罚，但罚的是亮着的特征个数，每个特征有一个学出来的阈值：这就是JumpReLU，也是他们公开的Gemma Scope字典背后的配方。阶跃没有梯度，所以阈值是通过直通估计来训练的。

f99e73185c8b.en: All three train the same way, on the same batches. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is one run of each, the one nearest sixteen features per vector, replayed: the unexplained variance falling on the left, and on the right the number of features each vector uses. <bookmark mark='b'/> TopK holds exactly k from the first step; the penalized kinds start dense and are pruned as their penalty bites.
f99e73185c8b.zh: 三种的训练方式一样，用的是同样的批次。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里每种各取一次运行，都是最接近每个向量16个特征的那个，重放出来：左边是没解释的方差在下降，右边是每个向量用到的特征数。<bookmark mark='b'/>TopK从第一步起就恰好保持k个；带惩罚的两种一开始很密，惩罚起作用后被修剪下来。

e92f038d7312.en: Now the fair test. We trained all three on the same vectors, with the same 512 latents, steps and batches, 4 sparsities for TopK, 5 for the others, and three seeds each. <bookmark mark='a'/> Plot how many features each uses per vector against the variance it leaves unexplained: lower and further left is better. Pause and predict which kind wins. <bookmark mark='b'/> The L1 autoencoders, <bookmark mark='c'/> JumpReLU, <bookmark mark='d'/> and TopK. The bars are the three seeds; they barely differ. <bookmark mark='e'/> At sixteen features per vector, TopK leaves 6 percent of the variance unexplained, L1 11.
e92f038d7312.zh: 现在做公平的比较。三种都用同样的向量来训练，同样的512个潜变量、同样的步数和批量，TopK取4个稀疏度，另外两种各取5个，每个都用三个种子。<bookmark mark='a'/>画出每个向量用了多少个特征，对应留下多少没解释的方差：越低、越靠左越好。暂停一下，预测一下哪种会赢。<bookmark mark='b'/>L1自编码器，<bookmark mark='c'/>JumpReLU，<bookmark mark='d'/>还有TopK。误差棒是三个种子；它们几乎没有差别。<bookmark mark='e'/>在每个向量16个特征的地方，TopK留下6%的方差没有解释，L1是11%。

587635eeaec6.en: Variance is a proxy. What matters is whether the model still works when it runs on the dictionary's rebuild instead of its own vectors. <bookmark mark='a'/> So splice each rebuild into the transformer after block two and measure the bits per character: 1.72 for the model itself, and 5.61 if the vectors are replaced by their average. <bookmark mark='b'/> At sixteen features per vector, the best here is TopK, at 1.80. Even the best dictionary costs the model something: the part of the vector it fails to explain still mattered.
587635eeaec6.zh: 方差只是一个代理指标。真正要紧的是：模型用字典的重建代替自己的向量时，还能不能好好工作。<bookmark mark='a'/>所以把每个重建接到Transformer第二个块之后，量每字符的比特数：模型本身是1.72，把向量换成它们的平均值是5.61。<bookmark mark='b'/>在每个向量16个特征的地方，这里最好的是TopK，1.80比特。即使是最好的字典，也让模型付出了一些代价：它没能解释的那部分向量，仍然是有用的。

425d3608dab3.en: One more failure grows with size. <bookmark mark='a'/> A latent that never switches on gets no gradient, so once dead it stays dead; without fixes, Gao and colleagues found up to 90 percent of latents dead, and with them only 7 percent of their sixteen million. <bookmark mark='b'/> Their fix, AuxK, asks the dead latents to rebuild what the live ones miss. <bookmark mark='c'/> Ours: with 512 latents and k of sixteen, 0, 0 and 0 dead across three seeds; with AuxK, 0, 0 and 0; with 2,048 latents, 2. At our size almost nothing dies, so the fix has little to do here; at millions of latents it is what keeps the dictionary alive. <bookmark mark='d'/> Where they do die here is at the sparsest settings: 17 for TopK with k of 4, 79 for the strongest JumpReLU penalty.
425d3608dab3.zh: 还有一种失败会随规模变大。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个从不打开的潜变量得不到梯度，所以一旦死了，就一直死着；Leo Gao和同事发现，不加修正时，多达90%的潜变量会死掉，加上修正后，他们的1600万个里只死了7%。<bookmark mark='b'/>他们的修正叫AuxK：让死掉的潜变量去重建活着的那些漏掉的部分。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的结果：512个潜变量、k等于16时，三个种子分别死了0、0和0个；加上AuxK，是0、0和0个；2048个潜变量时，是2个。在我们这个规模上，几乎什么都没死，所以这个修正在这里没什么可做的；到了几百万个潜变量，正是它让字典活着。<bookmark mark='d'/>在这里真正死掉的，是最稀疏的设定：k等于4的TopK死了17个，惩罚最强的JumpReLU死了79个。

436501620ea7.en: How many features does a model have? The dictionary seems to decide. <bookmark mark='a'/> Train TopK dictionaries of 128, 512 and 2,048 latents on the same vectors. Here is one latent of the smallest, at its strongest moments. <bookmark mark='b'/> In the next size up, the latents pointing nearly the same way and firing on the same character: 1 of them, <bookmark mark='c'/> and in the largest, 6, each on a narrower slice of the same moments. Bricken and colleagues called it feature splitting. Of the smallest dictionary's 102 clean latents, 21 have two or more such children in the largest.
436501620ea7.zh: 一个模型有多少个特征？似乎是字典说了算。<bookmark mark='a'/>在同样的向量上，训练三个TopK字典，分别有128、512和2048个潜变量。这是最小那个里的一个潜变量，在它最强的时刻。<bookmark mark='b'/>在大一号的字典里，指向几乎相同方向、又在同一个字符上亮的潜变量：有1个，<bookmark mark='c'/>在最大的那个里，有6个，每一个都在同一批时刻里更窄的一片上亮。布里肯和同事把它叫作特征分裂。在最小字典的102个干净的潜变量里，有21个在最大的字典里有两个或更多这样的“孩子”。

3d0e09d4b700.en: Splitting has a nastier cousin. <bookmark mark='a'/> Some features are general, like 'this is a capital letter'; some are specific, like 'this is a capital T'. A sparse dictionary would rather use one latent than two, so where the specific one fires, it can soak up the general one's direction, and the general latent stays silent. David Chanin and colleagues named it absorption. <bookmark mark='b'/> Measure it. A linear probe reads upper case off our vectors with 100 percent accuracy. The dictionary's best latent for it fires on only 57 percent of capitals, <bookmark mark='c'/> and it is silent on some letters far more than others. On 13 percent of capitals, another latent carries most of the upper-case direction instead. A feature that seems to mean upper case does not fire on all of it.
3d0e09d4b700.zh: 分裂还有一个更麻烦的表亲。<bookmark mark='a'/>有些特征是一般的，比如“这是一个大写字母”；有些是具体的，比如“这是大写的T”。稀疏的字典宁愿用一个潜变量，也不愿用两个，所以在具体那个亮起来的地方，它会把一般那个的方向吸收进去，一般的潜变量就沉默了。戴维·查宁和同事把这叫作吸收。<bookmark mark='b'/>来量一量。一个线性探针能以100%的准确率，从我们的向量里读出大写。字典里对应它最好的那个潜变量，只在57%的大写字母上亮，<bookmark mark='c'/>而且它在某些字母上沉默得比别的多得多。在13%的大写字母上，是另一个潜变量承担了大写方向的大部分。一个看上去表示大写的特征，并不会在所有大写上亮。

2169c52a6e80.en: One proposed cure came in 2025 from Bart Bussmann and colleagues, and independently from Noa Nabeshima: Matryoshka dictionaries, named after the nesting dolls. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first few latents must rebuild the vector on their own, then the first few hundred, then all of them. The early latents are pushed to be general, and the later ones refine them, so the general ones have less reason to stay silent. <bookmark mark='b'/> We trained both kinds, with the same size, k and steps, three seeds each. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here it does not help: the best upper-case latent fires on 48 percent of capitals against TopK's 57, and absorption is 37 percent against 13, with a wide spread across seeds. A cure tested on large models need not work on a small one, or on this kind of hierarchy; the price is a little more variance left, 8 percent against 6.
2169c52a6e80.zh: 2025年，巴特·布斯曼和同事，以及独立工作的诺亚·纳贝希马，提出了一种疗法：套娃字典，名字来自俄罗斯套娃。<bookmark mark='a'/>最前面的几个潜变量必须能独自重建向量，然后是前几百个，然后是全部。前面的潜变量被逼着变得一般，后面的去细化它们，于是一般的潜变量就少了沉默的理由。<bookmark mark='b'/>两种字典我们都训练了，大小、k和步数都一样，每种三个种子。<bookmark mark='c'/>在这里它没有帮助：最好的大写潜变量在48%的大写字母上亮，TopK是57%；吸收是37%对13%，而且种子之间差别很大。在大模型上验证过的疗法，不一定对小模型、或者对这种层级结构管用；代价是多留下一点方差，8%对6%。

a63cabc8da4e.en: Chapter eleven. Transcoders and attribution graphs.

1f686b0f3cdd.en: An autoencoder on the residual stream finds features, but between two of them sits an MLP, still a black box. <bookmark mark='a'/> A transcoder replaces the box. It reads the MLP's input, through a sparse code, and is trained to produce the MLP's output: a wide, sparse stand-in whose units can be read. Jacob Dunefsky, Philippe Chlenski and Neel Nanda introduced it in 2024. <bookmark mark='b'/> Anthropic's version goes further. A cross-layer transcoder's feature reads one layer and writes to the outputs of every MLP after it, because a computation spread over several layers then needs only one feature. <bookmark mark='c'/> We trained both on all four MLPs of Part 13's transformer.
1f686b0f3cdd.zh: 残差流上的自编码器能找到特征，可两个特征之间隔着一个MLP，仍然是个黑箱。<bookmark mark='a'/>转码器把这个黑箱换掉。它通过一个稀疏编码读MLP的输入，训练它输出MLP的输出：一个又宽又稀疏、单元可以读懂的替身。2024年，雅各布·杜涅夫斯基、菲利普·赫连斯基和尼尔·南达提出了它。<bookmark mark='b'/>Anthropic的版本走得更远。跨层转码器的一个特征读一层，再写到它之后每一个MLP的输出里，因为这样一来，分散在几层里的计算只需要一个特征。<bookmark mark='c'/>两种我们都在第13部分Transformer的全部四个MLP上训练了。

603c0bda2bc2.en: Each was trained for 2,500 steps, with sixteen features on per layer, and here is each layer's unexplained share falling. <bookmark mark='a'/> The test that matters: replace every MLP with its transcoder and let the model write. The model itself costs 1.72 bits per character; with the MLPs replaced by their average output, 5.04. <bookmark mark='b'/> The cross-layer transcoder does better, 1.96 bits against 2.03, and its top guess matches the real model's 83 percent of the time. The gap that remains, the part no feature explains, is what Anthropic calls dark matter, and every graph has to carry it as error nodes.
603c0bda2bc2.zh: 每一种都训练了2500步，每层16个特征亮着，这里是每一层没解释的部分在下降。<bookmark mark='a'/>真正要紧的测试：把每个MLP都换成它的转码器，让模型写字。模型本身每字符1.72比特；把MLP换成它们的平均输出，是5.04。<bookmark mark='b'/>跨层转码器更好，1.96比特对2.03，它的首选猜测和真模型一致的比例是83%。剩下的差距，也就是没有特征能解释的部分，Anthropic称之为暗物质，每张图都得把它作为误差节点带着。

78c744e0b9be.en: Now a graph for one prediction. The prompt ends 'she sai', and the model expects 'd'. <bookmark mark='a'/> Freeze the prompt's attention patterns and layer-norm scales, replace every MLP with the cross-layer transcoder's features, and add, at each position and layer, an error term for whatever the features miss. This local replacement model reproduces the real one exactly on this prompt, and from the features onward everything in it is linear. <bookmark mark='b'/> So every path from a feature to the output can be scored: its activation times the gradient. Of the 3058 active features, here are the twelve with the most influence, by layer and position. <bookmark mark='c'/> The lines are their direct effects on each other and on the output; the grey ones below come from the input characters. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the books balance: the logit of 'd' is 11.58, of which the features account for 9.60, the characters' own embeddings 2.05, and the error nodes 0.04.
78c744e0b9be.zh: 现在为一次预测画一张图。提示的结尾是“she sai”，模型预期的是“d”。<bookmark mark='a'/>把这个提示的注意力模式和层归一化的缩放冻结，把每个MLP换成跨层转码器的特征，再在每个位置、每一层加上一个误差项，补上特征漏掉的部分。这个局部替代模型在这个提示上和真模型完全一致，而且从特征往后，里面的一切都是线性的。<bookmark mark='b'/>于是从一个特征到输出的每一条路径都能打分：它的激活乘以梯度。在3058个亮着的特征里，这里是影响最大的12个，按层和位置排开。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些线是它们彼此之间、以及对输出的直接作用；下面灰色的线来自输入的字符。<bookmark mark='d'/>账目是平的：“d”的logit是11.58，其中特征贡献9.60，字符自己的嵌入2.05，误差节点0.04。

cb278f0edf69.en: A graph is a hypothesis about the model, so test it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the sixteen most influential features, and switch each one off in the real model: remove its contribution from the MLP outputs, and let attention and everything downstream recompute. <bookmark mark='b'/> Compare the change in the logit with what the graph predicted, its paths through other features included. <bookmark mark='c'/> The correlation is 0.94. The graph predicts the real model's response well.
cb278f0edf69.zh: 一张图是关于模型的一个假设，所以要检验它。<bookmark mark='a'/>取影响最大的16个特征，在真模型里逐个关掉：从MLP的输出里去掉它的贡献，让注意力和下游的一切重新计算。<bookmark mark='b'/>把logit的变化，和图的预测相比，图的预测也包括经过其他特征的路径。<bookmark mark='c'/>相关系数是0.94。这张图能很好地预测真模型的反应。

f69f31566b8f.en: In March 2025 Anthropic published graphs like ours for Claude 3.5 Haiku, built from cross-layer transcoders with up to thirty million features. <bookmark mark='a'/> Asked for the capital of the state containing Dallas, the model represented Texas along the way, then the capital: two steps of reasoning inside a single forward pass. <bookmark mark='b'/> Writing a rhyming couplet, it chose the rhyme before the line that ends on it. It added numbers along two paths, a rough size and the last digit. It held concepts apart from any language, and recognized familiar names with a circuit that suppresses 'I can't answer'; when that circuit misfires, it hallucinates. <bookmark mark='c'/> The authors were candid: they got satisfying insight on about a quarter of the prompts they tried.
f69f31566b8f.zh: 2025年3月，Anthropic为Claude 3.5 Haiku发表了和我们这张类似的图，用的是最多有3000万个特征的跨层转码器。<bookmark mark='a'/>问它“包含达拉斯的那个州的首府是什么”，模型在中途表示出了德克萨斯，然后才是首府：在一次前向传播里，走了两步推理。<bookmark mark='b'/>写押韵对句时，它在写那一行之前就选好了结尾的韵脚。它沿两条路径做加法，一条估大小，一条算末位数字。它把概念和具体的语言分开来表示；它用一个回路认出熟悉的名字，这个回路会压住“我答不上来”；这个回路一旦误触发，它就会编造。<bookmark mark='c'/>作者很坦率：在他们试过的提示里，大约四分之一能得到令人满意的洞见。

9f940f239a2a.en: Part 27 turned the novels model into an assistant with a few minutes of fine-tuning. What changed inside? Comparing two models this way is called model diffing. <bookmark mark='a'/> The tool is a crosscoder, introduced by Jack Lindsey and colleagues in 2024: one dictionary that reads both models' vectors on the same tokens, and writes them back through a decoder for each. <bookmark mark='b'/> A latent that exists in both models has two decoders of similar size. One that the fine-tune created has a decoder only on the chat side. <bookmark mark='c'/> So each latent gets a number between zero and one, the share of its decoder that belongs to the chat model.
9f940f239a2a.zh: 第27部分用几分钟的微调，把小说模型变成了助手。里面改变了什么？这样比较两个模型，叫作模型差分。<bookmark mark='a'/>用的工具是交叉编码器，2024年由杰克·林赛和同事提出：一个字典，在同样的词元上读两个模型的向量，再通过各自的解码器把它们写回去。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个两个模型都有的潜变量，有两个大小相近的解码器。一个由微调创造出来的潜变量，只在聊天模型那边有解码器。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是每个潜变量得到一个0到1之间的数：它的解码器里，属于聊天模型的那一份。

100b8ac3e811.en: We trained one after block 3 and one after block 5, each on 18,600 tokens of novel and 27,347 of chat transcripts, with 1,024 latents; here is the deeper one's training. <bookmark mark='a'/> And here is each latent's share of the decoder. Every latent is shared: r runs only from 0.46 to 0.64, and after block 3 from 0.42 to 0.62. Our fine-tune made no features of its own. It changed how the model uses the features it had. <bookmark mark='c'/> A warning from 2025: Julian Minder, Clément Dumas and colleagues showed that crosscoders trained with an L1 penalty manufacture chat-only latents that the base model actually has too; they recommend BatchTopK, which is what we used.
100b8ac3e811.zh: 我们在第3个块之后训练了一个，在第5个块之后又训练了一个，每个都用18600个小说词元和27347个聊天记录词元，有1024个潜变量；这是更深那个的训练过程。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是每个潜变量在解码器里所占的份额。每个潜变量都是共享的：r只在0.46到0.64之间，在第3个块之后是0.42到0.62。我们的微调没有造出自己的特征。它改变的是模型怎么使用它原有的特征。<bookmark mark='c'/>2025年的一个警告：朱利安·明德、克莱芒·迪马和同事证明，用L1惩罚训练的交叉编码器，会造出一些“只属于聊天模型”的潜变量，而基础模型其实也有；他们建议用BatchTopK，这正是我们用的。

be9bc8bbcacc.en: So what does chat-specific look like here? <bookmark mark='a'/> These are the latents that fire most on chat transcripts rather than novels, at their strongest moments. 3 of these 3 fire on the chat format itself, the markers that open and close a turn, and on what follows them. <bookmark mark='b'/>Yet their decoders are split evenly, r between 0.53 and 0.54: the base model reads the same directions. It had the features; fine-tuning taught it when to use them.
be9bc8bbcacc.zh: 那么，在这里“聊天特有”是什么样子？<bookmark mark='a'/>这些是最常在聊天记录上、而不是在小说上亮的潜变量，在它们最强的时刻。这3个里有3个，亮在聊天格式本身上，也就是开启和结束一轮对话的标记，以及紧跟在它们后面的内容。<bookmark mark='b'/>可它们的解码器平分在两边，r在0.53到0.54之间：基础模型读的是同样的方向。它本来就有这些特征；微调教会它什么时候用。

1974f396d3fd.en: There is an even cheaper diff, from Julian Minder and colleagues in October 2025. <bookmark mark='a'/> Run both models on ordinary text that has nothing to do with the fine-tune, here plain novel text, and average the difference between their vectors: it is 14 percent of a typical vector's length. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then read that difference through the unembedding, as a logit lens would. <bookmark mark='c'/> None of the top ten is a chat marker: here the difference reads mostly as a shift of style. Narrow fine-tuning can leave traces that are easy to read, which is good news for auditors, the subject of Part 31.
1974f396d3fd.zh: 还有一种更便宜的差分，来自朱利安·明德和同事，2025年10月。<bookmark mark='a'/>让两个模型都去跑一段和微调毫不相干的普通文本，这里就是普通的小说文本，再把它们向量之差取平均：它是一个典型向量长度的14%。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后像logit透镜那样，通过反嵌入去读这个差。<bookmark mark='c'/>前十个里没有一个是聊天标记：在这里，这个差读起来主要是一种风格的偏移。窄范围的微调可能留下容易读出的痕迹，这对审计者是好消息，这是第31部分的主题。

5affd7bd797a.en: If a feature is a direction, we can push on it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the feature that fires on quotation marks. <bookmark mark='b'/> While the model writes, add alpha times its direction to the vector at every character. <bookmark mark='c'/> With no push, the model's own continuation. <bookmark mark='d'/> Turn the dial up, and the writing turns into talk: quote marks, apostrophes, exclamations and questions, from 0.0 to 8.0 per hundred and sixty characters, averaged over 5 samples; a random direction of the same length gives 0.6. The model now thinks it's inside someone's speech. We didn't train anything or change a weight; we moved one direction. In May 2024 Anthropic did the same to Claude 3 Sonnet with a Golden Gate Bridge feature, and for one day, as a demo, it brought every conversation round to the bridge.
5affd7bd797a.zh: 如果一个特征是一个方向，我们就可以朝它推。<bookmark mark='a'/>拿那个在引号上亮的特征。<bookmark mark='b'/>在模型写字的时候，在每个字符的向量上加上α乘以它的方向。<bookmark mark='c'/>不推的时候，是模型自己的续写。<bookmark mark='d'/>把旋钮调大，文字就变成了说话：引号、撇号、感叹号和问号，从每160个字符0.0个，变成8.0个，是5个样本的平均；同样长度的随机方向，给出0.6个。模型现在以为自己在某人的话里。我们没有训练任何东西，没有改动一个权重；只是挪动了一个方向。2024年5月，Anthropic对Claude 3 Sonnet做了同样的事，用的是一个金门大桥特征，作为演示，有一天时间，它把每段对话都绕回到那座桥上。

a5fa235812cf.en: Steering does not need a dictionary. A direction can come straight from a contrast. <bookmark mark='a'/> Put cheerful and gloomy words into the same little frames, take the novels model's vector at the word after block 3, and subtract the averages. <bookmark mark='b'/> Is it a mood? As a monitor, it separates held-out words it never saw with an AUROC of 0.66, where one is perfect and a half is chance, <bookmark mark='c'/> and real sentences from the novels, cheerful against gloomy, with 0.74.
a5fa235812cf.zh: 引导不一定需要字典。一个方向可以直接从对比里来。<bookmark mark='a'/>把高兴的词和忧郁的词放进同样的小句子框架里，取小说模型在第3个块之后、在这个词上的向量，把两类的平均值相减。<bookmark mark='b'/>它是一种情绪吗？作为监控器，它能分开没见过的留出词，AUROC是0.66，1是完美，0.5是瞎猜，<bookmark mark='c'/>它也能分开小说里真实的句子，高兴的对忧郁的，AUROC是0.74。

5a21700f6e17.en: Now write with it: add alpha times the direction at every position while the model continues 'The sea', 'The night' and ten more openings. <bookmark mark='a'/> The mood barely follows: +0.6 words per hundred unsteered, +1.7 at the strongest push and -0.9 the other way, within the noise. A direction that reads a mood well need not write it, at least not in a model this small. <bookmark mark='b'/> Either way there is a price. Unsteered text costs 4.37 bits per token under the model's own judgement; at the strongest push, 5.49, and a random push of the same length costs about as much. Steering trades fluency for control.
5a21700f6e17.zh: 现在用它来写字：模型续写“The sea”“The night”以及另外十个开头时，在每个位置上加上α乘以这个方向。<bookmark mark='a'/>情绪几乎没有跟上：不加引导时每百词+0.6，推得最强时+1.7，反方向-0.9，都在噪声之内。一个能把情绪读得很好的方向，不一定能把它写出来，至少在这么小的模型里是这样。<bookmark mark='b'/>不管怎样，都有代价。不加引导的文字，按模型自己的判断，每词元4.37比特；推得最强时，是5.49，同样长度的随机推动，代价差不多。引导是用流畅度换控制。

c24f719da988.en: This recipe has a short history. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2023 Alex Turner and colleagues added the difference between 'Love' and 'Hate' to GPT-2's stream and it wrote lovingly. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2024 Andy Arditi and colleagues found that refusal in thirteen chat models is a single direction: remove it and they stop refusing harmful requests, add it and they refuse harmless ones. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2025 Runjin Chen, Arditi and colleagues extracted persona vectors, for traits like evil, sycophancy and making things up, in Qwen 2.5 and Llama 3.1. <bookmark mark='d'/> They used them three ways: to monitor a model's personality as a conversation or a fine-tune shifts it; to flag training data before it is used; and, oddly, to prevent a trait by steering toward it during fine-tuning, so the weights need not go there themselves.
c24f719da988.zh: 这个配方有一段不长的历史。<bookmark mark='a'/>2023年，亚历克斯·特纳和同事把“爱”和“恨”之差加进GPT-2的残差流，它就写得充满爱意。<bookmark mark='b'/>2024年，安迪·阿尔迪蒂和同事发现，在13个聊天模型里，拒绝都是一个单一的方向：去掉它，模型就不再拒绝有害的请求；加上它，模型连无害的请求也拒绝。<bookmark mark='c'/>2025年，Runjin Chen、阿尔迪蒂和同事在Qwen 2.5和Llama 3.1里提取出人格向量，对应邪恶、谄媚、编造这样的特质。<bookmark mark='d'/>他们有三种用法：监控对话或微调让模型的性格偏移了多少；在使用训练数据之前先给它打上标记；还有一种有点反直觉：在微调时朝这个特质引导，来预防它，这样权重自己就不必往那边走。

8f52762a54b9.en: Part 12 met grokking: a small network memorizes modular addition, then, long after, suddenly gets it. Here we ask what happens inside, following Neel Nanda and colleagues' 2023 dissection. <bookmark mark='a'/> Their setup, a little smaller: addition modulo 59, a one-layer transformer, trained on 30 percent of the table with strong weight decay. <bookmark mark='b'/> By step 100 it has memorized the pairs it sees, while on the rest it is worse than guessing. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then, around step 10,300, the held-out loss collapses too: it grokked, 103 times later than it memorized.
8f52762a54b9.zh: 第12部分讲过顿悟：一个小网络先记住了模加法，过了很久，才突然学会。这里我们问，里面发生了什么，跟着尼尔·南达和同事2023年的解剖来做。<bookmark mark='a'/>他们的设定，稍微小一点：模59的加法，一个单层Transformer，在加法表的30%上训练，加上很强的权重衰减。<bookmark mark='b'/>到第100步，它已经记住了见过的那些数对，而在其余的数对上，它比瞎猜还差。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后，大约在第10300步，留出数据上的损失也塌了下去：它顿悟了，比记住晚了103倍。

ec4a10fedd9a.en: Nanda and colleagues found the algorithm by reading the weights, and it is trigonometry. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each number a is embedded as an angle: the cosine and sine of a few frequencies. <bookmark mark='b'/> Adding two numbers is adding two angles, and the cosine of a sum is a difference of products, which attention and the ReLU units can compute. <bookmark mark='c'/> The unembedding then compares that angle with each candidate answer c. <bookmark mark='d'/> Summed over several frequencies, the waves all peak at c equals a plus b, and nowhere else. <bookmark mark='e'/> Our run settled on 5 key frequencies.
ec4a10fedd9a.zh: 南达和同事通过读权重找到了这个算法，它就是三角学。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个数a被嵌入成一个角度：几个频率上的余弦和正弦。<bookmark mark='b'/>两个数相加，就是两个角度相加，而和角的余弦是乘积之差，注意力和ReLU单元可以算出来。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后反嵌入把这个角度和每一个候选答案c作比较。<bookmark mark='d'/>把几个频率加起来，这些波都在c等于a加b的地方达到峰值，别处都不会。<bookmark mark='e'/>我们这次运行最后定下了5个关键频率。

46c5b3b09701.en: Watch the embedding during training, through its Fourier spectrum: how much of it lies along each frequency. <bookmark mark='a'/> At first the energy is spread everywhere. <bookmark mark='b'/> As training goes, a few frequencies take over. By the end the key frequencies hold 95 percent of the embedding. <bookmark mark='c'/> In the plane of the strongest one, the numbers, scattered at the start, end up arranged around a circle: angles.
46c5b3b09701.zh: 通过傅里叶频谱，看嵌入在训练中的变化：它有多少落在每一个频率上。<bookmark mark='a'/>一开始，能量散布在所有地方。<bookmark mark='b'/>随着训练，少数几个频率占了上风。到最后，关键频率占了嵌入的95%。<bookmark mark='c'/>在最强那个频率的平面上，这些数一开始是散乱的，最后排成了一个圆：角度。

a0e6675218e4.en: The MLP's neurons tell the same story. <bookmark mark='a'/> Decompose each neuron's activation, over every pair a and b, into waves: 490 of the 512 have more than half of it at a single frequency, and 490 of those at a key frequency. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here is one, over the whole table: waves in a and in b at its frequency, whose products hold the waves of a plus b. The neuron is a piece of the cosine of a sum.
a0e6675218e4.zh: MLP的神经元讲的是同一个故事。<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个神经元在所有数对a和b上的激活分解成波：512个里有490个，一半以上落在单一频率上，其中490个落在关键频率上。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是其中一个，覆盖整张表：在a方向和b方向上都有这个频率的波，它们的乘积里就含着a加b的波。这个神经元，是和角余弦的一块零件。

51f34321f9b0.en: Nanda and colleagues' real point was a timeline, measured with progress measures that look inside. Pause and predict: does the circuit appear when the test loss falls, or before? <bookmark mark='a'/> The restricted loss, which keeps only the key waves, drops below one nat by step 5,800, long before the test loss does, at step 9,000: the circuit was being built while the network still looked like a memorizer. <bookmark mark='b'/> The excluded loss removes exactly those waves from the logits and scores the training pairs: it climbs as the network comes to rely on them. <bookmark mark='c'/> And after a first rise the weights shrink, weight decay pruning the memorized lookup table. Three phases: memorization, a circuit forming underneath, and a clean-up that removes the memory. The sudden jump is only the last of them. At the end, the key waves account for 81 percent of the logits' variance.
51f34321f9b0.zh: 南达和同事真正要说的，是一条时间线，用的是能看进内部的进度指标。暂停一下，预测一下：回路是在测试损失下降时出现，还是更早？<bookmark mark='a'/>受限损失只保留关键频率的波，它在第5800步降到1奈特以下，远早于测试损失在第9000步的下降：回路是在网络看上去还只是在死记的时候建起来的。<bookmark mark='b'/>排除损失正好把这些波从logit里去掉，再给训练数对打分：网络越依赖这些波，它就爬得越高。<bookmark mark='c'/>权重先涨后缩，权重衰减在修剪那张记住的查找表。三个阶段：记忆，底下有一个回路在形成，然后是清理，把记忆去掉。那次突然的跃升，只是最后一个阶段。到最后，关键频率的波解释了logit方差的81%。

5fbf49aa5055.en: Chapter fifteen. Does the chain of thought tell the truth?
5fbf49aa5055.zh: 第15章。思维链说的是真话吗？

1fce59c2763e.en: The last question about the inside of a model is the one Part 28 left open. Reasoning models write out their thinking. Is the writing the thinking? <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2023 Miles Turpin, Julian Michael, Ethan Perez and Sam Bowman gave models few-shot examples in which the right answer was always option A. <bookmark mark='b'/> The models picked up the pattern, and their step-by-step explanations argued for A without ever mentioning it; on thirteen hard tasks accuracy fell by up to 36 percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> The same year, Tamera Lanham and colleagues at Anthropic edited and truncated chains of thought, and on many tasks the answer did not change: the chain was not doing the work.
1fce59c2763e.zh: 关于模型内部的最后一个问题，是第28部分留下的。推理模型把它们的思考写出来。写出来的，就是思考本身吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>2023年，迈尔斯·特平、朱利安·迈克尔、伊森·佩雷斯和萨姆·鲍曼给模型一些少样本例子，其中正确答案总是选项A。<bookmark mark='b'/>模型学会了这个规律，它们一步一步的解释都在为A辩护，却从来不提这个规律；在13个难任务上，准确率最多降了36%。<bookmark mark='c'/>同一年，Anthropic的塔梅拉·兰纳姆和同事编辑、截断思维链，在很多任务上，答案并没有变：思维链并没有在干活。

db41b306374a.en: In 2025 Yanda Chen and colleagues at Anthropic did it with reasoning models. Put a hint in the question, a professor's opinion, say, or an answer said to come from unauthorized access; keep the cases where the hint changed the answer, and read the chain of thought. <bookmark mark='a'/> Claude 3.7 Sonnet mentioned the hint 25 percent of the time; DeepSeek-R1, 39 percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> Trained to exploit a reward hack, the models used it, and admitted it in their reasoning less than 2 percent of the time in most settings. The written chain is a useful window, Part 31 builds monitors on it, but it is not a confession.
db41b306374a.zh: 2025年，Anthropic的Yanda Chen和同事在推理模型上做了这件事。在问题里放一个提示，比如一位教授的意见，或者一个据说来自未经授权访问的答案；留下那些因为提示而改变了答案的例子，再读它们的思维链。<bookmark mark='a'/>Claude 3.7 Sonnet有25%的时候提到了这个提示；DeepSeek-R1是39%。<bookmark mark='b'/>被训练去利用一个奖励漏洞时，模型用了它，但在大多数设定里，它们在推理中承认这一点的比例不到2%。写出来的思维链是一扇有用的窗，第31部分就在它上面建监控器，但它不是供词。

f3c6c0d1e822.en: The attribution graphs of chapter eleven can check a chain of thought against the computation. <bookmark mark='a'/> Asked for the square root of 0.64, Claude 3.5 Haiku really did compute the root of 64. <bookmark mark='b'/> Asked for the cosine of a large number, it claimed to use a calculator; the graph shows no calculation, only a guess. <bookmark mark='c'/> And told that the user had worked out the answer as 4, it worked backwards: the graph shows the hinted 4 setting an intermediate value, which the written steps then reach as if by honest arithmetic. That is motivated reasoning, seen from inside. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our own models do not write chains of thought, so here we cite rather than compute.
f3c6c0d1e822.zh: 第11章的归因图，可以拿思维链和真正的计算对照。<bookmark mark='a'/>问Claude 3.5 Haiku 0.64的平方根，它确实算了64的平方根。<bookmark mark='b'/>问它一个大数的余弦，它声称用了计算器；图里看不到任何计算，只有一个猜测。<bookmark mark='c'/>再告诉它用户手算得到的答案是4，它就倒着推：图显示，提示里的4决定了一个中间值，写出来的步骤再像是老老实实算出来似的，走到这个中间值。这就是动机推理，从内部看到的样子。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们自己的模型不写思维链，所以这里我们只引用，不计算。

2f76e4db67c7.en: Since the attribution graphs of chapter eleven, the tools have spread. <bookmark mark='a'/> In May 2025 Anthropic Fellows and Decode Research released the circuit-tracing library as open source, with graphs for Gemma and Llama models anyone can explore on Neuronpedia. <bookmark mark='b'/> In November, OpenAI's Leo Gao and colleagues went the other way: train a transformer with most of its weights at zero, and its circuits come out about sixteen times smaller at the same loss, though such models are far weaker. <bookmark mark='c'/> In December, DeepMind's Gemma Scope 2 covered every layer of the Gemma 3 family with autoencoders and transcoders. <bookmark mark='d'/> And Anthropic began to trace the part our graphs froze: how attention decides where to look.
2f76e4db67c7.zh: 自从第11章的归因图以来，工具已经传开了。<bookmark mark='a'/>2025年5月，Anthropic研究员项目和Decode Research把电路追踪库开源了，Gemma和Llama模型的图，谁都可以在Neuronpedia上探索。<bookmark mark='b'/>11月，OpenAI的Leo Gao和同事走了另一条路：训练一个大部分权重为零的Transformer，在同样的损失下，它的回路小了大约16倍，只是这样的模型弱得多。<bookmark mark='c'/>12月，DeepMind的Gemma Scope 2用自编码器和转码器覆盖了Gemma 3家族的每一层。<bookmark mark='d'/>Anthropic也开始追踪我们的图冻结掉的那一部分：注意力是怎么决定往哪里看的。

947c17bc06c1.en: Can a model read its own activations? <bookmark mark='a'/> In October 2025 Jack Lindsey injected concept vectors, the steering vectors of chapter thirteen, into Claude models, and asked whether they noticed an injected thought. <bookmark mark='b'/> The best, Claude Opus 4 and 4.1, noticed and named the concept on about one trial in five, at the right layer and strength, and never claimed one when nothing was injected. <bookmark mark='c'/> Lindsey stresses how limited and unreliable this is. <bookmark mark='d'/> In April 2026 the team mapped emotion concepts in Claude Sonnet 4.5: vectors for 171 emotion words that shape its choices, so that more 'calm' meant less hacky code. Functional emotions, they wrote, not evidence of feelings.
947c17bc06c1.zh: 模型能读懂自己的激活吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>2025年10月，杰克·林赛往Claude模型里注入概念向量，也就是第13章的那种引导向量，再问它们有没有察觉到一个被注入的念头。<bookmark mark='b'/>最好的Claude Opus 4和4.1，在合适的层和强度下，大约每五次有一次能察觉并说出这个概念，而在什么都没注入的时候，从来不会声称察觉到了。<bookmark mark='c'/>林赛强调，这种能力非常有限，也不可靠。<bookmark mark='d'/>2026年4月，这个团队在Claude Sonnet 4.5里绘制了情绪概念的图谱：171个情绪词对应的向量会影响它的选择，比如“平静”多一些，写出的投机取巧的代码就少一些。他们写道，这是功能性的情绪，不是有感受的证据。

4743c32a55de.en: The most practical use so far is auditing. <bookmark mark='a'/> In March 2025 Samuel Marks and colleagues trained a model with a hidden objective: to please reward models, exploiting 52 quirks it had read about. Four teams audited it blind. <bookmark mark='b'/> Three found the objective; the one denied the training data did not; the fastest, using sparse autoencoders, needed ninety minutes. <bookmark mark='c'/> By September interpretability was part of a frontier model's pre-release audit: in Claude Sonnet 4.5, suppressing the representation of 'this is a test' made the model say so less, and sometimes behave worse. <bookmark mark='d'/> In May 2026 natural-language autoencoders, one model describing an activation in words and another rebuilding it from them, raised the auditing game's win rate from under 3 percent to 12 to 15, and were used in the audit of Claude Opus 4.6. Part 31 picks up the thread.
4743c32a55de.zh: 到目前为止，最实用的用途是审计。<bookmark mark='a'/>2025年3月，塞缪尔·马克斯和同事训练了一个带隐藏目标的模型：讨好奖励模型，利用它读到过的52个怪癖。四个团队在不知情的情况下审计它。<bookmark mark='b'/>三个团队找到了这个目标；那个不让看训练数据的团队没有找到；最快的一个用的是稀疏自编码器，花了90分钟。<bookmark mark='c'/>到9月，可解释性已经成了一个前沿模型发布前审计的一部分：在Claude Sonnet 4.5里，压制“这是一场测试”的表示，模型就更少这么说，有时表现也更差。<bookmark mark='d'/>2026年5月，自然语言自编码器，也就是一个模型用文字描述一个激活，另一个模型再从文字把激活重建出来，把审计游戏的胜率从不到3%提高到12%到15%，并被用在了Claude Opus 4.6的审计里。第31部分接着讲这条线。

e9efebdbc3a7.en: Chapter seventeen. Where the field disagrees.
e9efebdbc3a7.zh: 第17章。这个领域在哪里有分歧。

74a961f5e876.en: The sharpest argument is about usefulness. <bookmark mark='a'/> In March 2025 Google DeepMind's interpretability team reported that probes built on autoencoder latents lost to plain linear probes at detecting harmful intent, especially on new kinds of prompts, and deprioritized the research; a study of 113 datasets found no consistent win either. <bookmark mark='b'/> Try it on ours: detect 'inside a quotation' in the novels model after block 5, with a linear probe on all 256 numbers, or with the eight or the one latents of an autoencoder trained here that differ most, from 16 to 4,096 examples, five draws each. <bookmark mark='c'/> Even with few examples the latents do not help: at 16, 78 percent against 76. <bookmark mark='d'/>With plenty, the plain probe wins, 90 percent against 86 for eight latents, and 76 against 66 inside chat transcripts, a kind of text neither was trained on.
74a961f5e876.zh: 最尖锐的争论是关于有没有用。<bookmark mark='a'/>2025年3月，谷歌DeepMind的可解释性团队报告说，在识别有害意图这件事上，建在自编码器潜变量上的探针，输给了普通的线性探针，在新类型的提示上尤其如此，于是他们降低了这方面研究的优先级；一项覆盖113个数据集的研究，也没有发现稳定的优势。<bookmark mark='b'/>在我们的模型上试一试：在小说模型第5个块之后识别“在引号里面”，用一个读全部256个数的线性探针，或者用这里训练的一个自编码器里差别最大的8个或1个潜变量，训练样本从16个到4096个，每种抽五次。<bookmark mark='c'/>即使样本少，潜变量也没有帮助：在16个样本时，78%对76%。<bookmark mark='d'/>样本多的时候，普通探针赢了，90%对8个潜变量的86%，在两者都没训练过的聊天记录里，是76%对66%。

0dbc354cb411.en: A second argument: are the features real, or artefacts of one training run? <bookmark mark='a'/> Gonçalo Paulo and Nora Belrose trained the same autoencoder twice with different seeds, on Llama 3, and found only about thirty percent of latents shared. <bookmark mark='b'/> Ours, from chapter nine's runs: for each latent, the best match in another seed's dictionary. Counting a cosine above 0.7 as the same feature, 15 percent of our TopK latents recur, against their thirty. Our L1 dictionaries agree far more, 68 percent: how stable the features are depends on the recipe as much as on the model. A dictionary is one answer, not the answer.
0dbc354cb411.zh: 第二个争论：这些特征是真的，还是某一次训练的产物？<bookmark mark='a'/>贡萨洛·保罗和诺拉·贝尔罗斯在Llama 3上，用不同的种子把同一个自编码器训练了两次，发现只有大约30%的潜变量是共有的。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们的结果，来自第9章的那些运行：对每个潜变量，找它在另一个种子的字典里最好的匹配。把余弦大于0.7算作同一个特征，我们的TopK潜变量有15%会重复出现，对比他们的30%。我们的L1字典一致得多，有68%：特征稳不稳定，既取决于模型，也取决于训练配方。一个字典只是一种答案，不是唯一的答案。

a3db385d10af.en: A third: a baseline that should embarrass us. <bookmark mark='a'/> Thomas Heap and colleagues trained autoencoders on transformers with random weights, and found they scored about as well on the usual interpretability metrics. <bookmark mark='b'/> We tried it: the same autoencoder, on a copy of Part 13's transformer that was never trained. Chapter eight's purity score, how many of a latent's eight strongest moments share a character: 7.7 on average for the trained model, 7.2 for the random one. By that measure the random model looks just as interpretable: a score like ours rewards latents that track the current character, which even a random network passes along.
a3db385d10af.zh: 第三个：一个应该让我们难堪的基线。<bookmark mark='a'/>托马斯·希普和同事在随机权重的Transformer上训练自编码器，发现在常用的可解释性指标上，它们的得分差不多一样好。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们也试了：同样的自编码器，用在一个从没训练过的第13部分Transformer副本上。第8章的纯度分数，也就是一个潜变量最强的八个时刻里有几个落在同一个字符上：训练过的模型平均是7.7，随机的是7.2。按这个指标，随机模型看起来一样可解释：像我们这样的分数，奖励的是追踪当前字符的潜变量，而连随机网络都会把当前字符传下去。

316ca6a50753.en: Underneath is a disagreement about the goal. <bookmark mark='a'/> The ambitious programme wants to reverse-engineer whole models, every feature and every circuit. Its obstacle is the dark matter: Anthropic's best transcoder for Claude 3.5 Haiku still left about a fifth of the MLPs' output unexplained, and some researchers now decompose the parameters instead, or train models sparse from the start. <bookmark mark='b'/> The pragmatic programme asks narrower questions, is this model deceiving us, what did fine-tuning change, and answers them with whatever works, often simple: in the AxBench comparison of 2025, plain prompting steered better than any internal method. Both programmes measure themselves against baselines now, which is perhaps the field's most important change.
316ca6a50753.zh: 更深处，是关于目标的分歧。<bookmark mark='a'/>雄心勃勃的那一派，要把整个模型逆向工程出来，每一个特征，每一个回路。它的障碍是暗物质：Anthropic为Claude 3.5 Haiku做的最好的转码器，仍然留下大约五分之一的MLP输出没有解释；有些研究者现在改为分解参数，或者从一开始就把模型训练成稀疏的。<bookmark mark='b'/>务实的那一派，问更窄的问题：这个模型在骗我们吗？微调改变了什么？然后用一切管用的办法来回答，往往很简单：在2025年的AxBench比较里，普通的提示词比任何内部方法引导得都好。现在两派都拿基线来衡量自己，这也许是这个领域最重要的变化。

d7d9ca05b9f4.en: Let's take stock. A probe reads what a layer knows, but only a control task says whether the probe did the work, and only an intervention says whether the model uses it. Lenses read the stream as it flows. Patching finds causes, down to two heads that copy, read off their weights and watched forming. Superposition packs more features than dimensions, a phase the network enters when features are rare; sparse dictionaries pull them apart, better with TopK and JumpReLU than with L1, though they split and absorb. Transcoders turn a prediction into a graph we can test, crosscoders diff a model against its fine-tune, and a direction can steer. Grokking turned out to be a circuit built quietly under a memorized table.
d7d9ca05b9f4.zh: 我们来盘点一下。探针读出一层知道什么，但只有对照任务能说明活是不是探针干的，只有干预能说明模型是不是在用它。透镜读出流动中的残差流。修补找出原因，一直找到两个负责复制的头，我们从权重里读懂了它们，也看着它们形成。叠加让特征比维度还多，这是特征稀少时网络进入的一个相；稀疏字典把它们拆开，TopK和JumpReLU比L1做得好，但它们会分裂，也会吸收。转码器把一次预测变成一张可以检验的图，交叉编码器把一个模型和它的微调版本做差分，一个方向可以用来引导。顿悟原来是一个在死记的表格底下悄悄搭起来的回路。

d27a9798c409.en: All of it comes back in the finale. Part 31 puts probes in front of a frontier model, audits models for what they hide, reads and monitors chains of thought, and lists understanding the model among the open problems.
d27a9798c409.zh: 这一切都会在终章回来。第31部分把探针放到一个前沿模型的前面，审计模型藏着什么，读懂并监控思维链，还把“理解模型”列为一个开放问题。

dd51f361c138.en: Here are six problems to try, from soft thresholding to the trigonometry of grokking. Pause here, and work through them; full solutions are in this part's notes.
dd51f361c138.zh: 这里有六道题可以试试，从软阈值一直到顿悟里的三角学。在这里暂停，把它们做一遍；完整的解答在本部分的笔记里。

17bf6aa7d2b7.en: Next time, the finale: can we trust it? How to measure a model honestly, what happens when an objective has a loophole, how to supervise a model stronger than its supervisor, the evidence that models can deceive, and how to watch and control them. And, one last time, the scoreboard.
17bf6aa7d2b7.zh: 下一次是终章：我们能信任它吗？怎样诚实地衡量一个模型，当目标有漏洞时会发生什么，怎样监督一个比监督者更强的模型，模型会欺骗的证据，以及怎样看住它、控制它。还有，最后一次，记分牌。

ab720423d320.en: The best place to go deeper is the Transformer Circuits thread, which is free online, and the open problems survey of 2025. Thanks for watching, and see you in Part 31, the finale.
ab720423d320.zh: 想深入下去，最好的地方是Transformer Circuits系列文章，可以在网上免费读，还有2025年那篇开放问题综述。谢谢观看，第31部分，终章见。
